stem: Two canopy strategies produce similar total plant biomass, but one produces more uniform light penetration and cannabinoid distribution from upper to lower inflorescences. If product uniformity is the stated goal, which evaluation is strongest?
choices: Prefer the strategy with better spatial uniformity, then confirm that whole-cycle yield and plant response remain acceptable
Treat the strategies as equivalent because similar total biomass is the strongest indicator of comparable product uniformity
Prefer the strategy with greater upper-canopy exposure because lower-canopy chemical variation is unlikely to affect uniformity
Choose the strategy that removes more tissue because the extent of tissue removal is the best proxy for canopy uniformity
rationale: Plant-architecture research shows that light penetration and canopy position can affect within-plant cannabinoid uniformity. Evaluation should therefore use metrics aligned with the stated production objective instead of relying on total biomass alone.
